headline: Koninika Mitra joins SBS India as head-HR
summary: SBS India has appointed Koninika Mitra as its new head of human resources to lead the organization's workforce and people strategy. An alumna of XLRI Jamshedpur, Mitra brings over 20 years of experience across multiple sectors, including a recent six-year tenure as an HR vertical leader at Amazon. Her career also features HR leadership roles at prominent firms such as Honeywell, Times Internet, HSBC, and Lehman Brothers.

headline: Bank of America to hire 1,000 apprentices by 2028
summary: Bank of America plans to hire 1,000 additional apprentices over the next two years and commit $150 million to workforce development organizations over five years. The initiative expands the bank's skills-based hiring strategy, focusing on non-traditional career pathways that do not require a bachelor's degree. This announcement builds on existing commitments to recruit military veterans and community college graduates.

headline: Railways notifies Unified Pension Scheme rules for NPS-covered employees
summary: The Ministry of Railways has notified guidelines for the Unified Pension Scheme (UPS) targeting National Pension System-covered employees appointed on or after January 1, 2004. Under the new framework, employees completing 25 years of service are guaranteed a full pension equal to 50 percent of their average basic pay during their final 12 months. The scheme features a joint contribution model and provides employees a one-time, irreversible option to switch back to the NPS during their tenure.

headline: Pavitra Singh joins Burma Burma board
summary: Pavitra Singh, CHRO and Vice President of PepsiCo India & South Asia, has joined the board of Burma Burma Restaurant & Tea Room. Bringing over two decades of human resources experience, Singh will assist the growing restaurant chain with organizational scaling, frontline workforce strategy, and leadership development. Operated by Hunger Pangs, Burma Burma currently runs 13 restaurants and delivery kitchens across India.

headline: Central employees to get September salaries early amid bank strike
summary: Central government employees and pensioners will receive their September salaries early on September 25 to avoid disruptions from an upcoming nationwide bank strike. Organized by bank unions demanding a five-day work week, the three-day strike threatens branch-based banking services from September 28 to 30. The early disbursement will act as an advance payment, with any balance adjustments to be made in October.

headline: Amazon reaches out to former employees for AI, ML and cloud roles
summary: Amazon is actively recruiting former employees, including those previously laid off, to fill specialized roles in artificial intelligence, machine learning, and cloud computing. The targeted outreach follows major corporate workforce reductions and reflects a strategic rebalancing toward high-demand tech capabilities outlined by CEO Andy Jassy. Amazon noted that engaging alumni is a longstanding practice and does not signal a reversal of its overall headcount cuts.

headline: Culture takes years to build. It can break in hours
summary: As artificial intelligence reshapes modern workplaces, maintaining trust between employees, management, and automated systems is becoming increasingly critical. Speaking at an industry event, India Glycols CHRO Dev Jha emphasized that while organizational culture takes years to build, it can be rapidly damaged during technological shifts. To successfully integrate AI, companies must proactively monitor and protect workplace trust before cultural damage occurs.
